The “Magic” 5-Part Formula (Role + Task + Context + Format + Constraints)

🕵️‍♀️Role: Expert level (e.g., “Act as a PhD researcher”).
Task: The core objective (e.g., “Summarize this paper”)

🔬Context: Why you need this (e.g., “for a literature review section”)

🤖Format: The visual structure (e.g., “Bulleted list”)

🛑Constraints: Limits (e.g., “Keep it under 300 words” or “Don’t use jargon”)

Use this formula while drafting any prompt and you will instantly get better outputs.

Attention Is All You Need.

The research paper that changed the world.

Published by Google researchers in 2017, it introduced the Transformer architecture and proved that AI could understand relationships in text using attention, without relying on RNNs or LSTMs.

Today, almost every major language model, including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama and many others, is built on ideas that came from this paper.

A few fun facts:
• It has been cited hundreds of thousands of times, making it one of the most influential AI papers ever.
• The paper had 8 authors, often called the “Transformer Eight.”
• The famous title almost sounds like a Beatles reference: All You Need Is Love.
• The original model was trained to translate between languages, but the same architecture ended up powering modern generative AI.

Sometimes, one paper doesn’t just improve a field.

It creates an entirely new era.

I found out recently and honestly felt a bit behind, so sharing everything here:

→ Memory is not one switch, it’s two. One only saves what you tell it to save, so you actually have to say “add this to memory.” The other is called reference chat history and it quietly studies everything you’ve ever typed, even the stuff you never asked it to remember.

→ Custom instructions let you tell ChatGPT who you are and how you want it to talk. Do this once and every future reply already sounds like it knows you.

→ On iPhone, ChatGPT can sit inside Siri through Apple Intelligence. Sign in once and Siri hands your hardest questions straight to ChatGPT.

→ There’s an apps and connectors option in the sidebar that lets you plug your tools directly into your chats.

→ Data controls let you turn off “improve the model for everyone” so your conversations stop training it. And if all this memory talk freaked you out a little, there’s a temporary chat option that remembers nothing at all.

These settings are sitting inside your app right now and almost nobody has opened that tab.
